claims.text: The starting catalyst is a multi-element automotive alloy with nearly equiatomic principal elements and low platinum-group-metal content.
A thin, conformal CeO2 overlayer can be deposited on the catalyst surface, for example by atomic layer deposition.
The deposited CeO2 layer will be uniform and nanometer-scale.
The CeO2 overlayer will provide oxygen-storage and oxygen-release functionality.
The oxygen-storage and release functionality of the CeO2 overlayer will buffer the local redox environment under fluctuating exhaust conditions.
The CeO2 overlayer will inhibit local sintering of the catalyst.
The CeO2 overlayer will limit migration of active sites.
The CeO2 overlayer will maintain a protective surface structure under fluctuating exhaust conditions.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the CeO2-coated catalyst will have a lower low-temperature light-off temperature.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the CeO2-coated catalyst will have higher low-temperature conversion rates.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the CeO2-coated catalyst will undergo slower activity degradation during thermal aging.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the CeO2-coated catalyst will undergo slower activity degradation during exposure to H2O and NO.
Adding the CeO2 overlayer will preserve low platinum-group-metal consumption.
The untreated multi-element alloy catalyst typically experiences significant activity loss and durability limitations under the stated exhaust conditions.
The proposed benefits are expected under transient, low-temperature operation with controlled H2O and NO exposure and moderate thermal aging.
